angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 423,681 km at 193.11 pc = 0.03 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.1783 +/- 0.0168 mas (same row, RUWE 1.10): 193.11 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.609 +/- 0.015 solar radii from Premnath et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-7394 B b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....172...92P/abstract): 423,681 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.624 +/- 0.022 solar masses from Premnath et al. 2026, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-7394 B b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....172...92P/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3717 +/- 59 K from Premnath et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-7394 B b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....172...92P/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Premnath et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-7394 B b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....172...92P/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-7394-b.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.664, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
